title: Chapter 26
content:
The white sports car roared, tearing down the road at breakneck speed. Ahead of it, the motorcycle danced just within reach, baiting and teasing like a phantom. As the chase dragged on, the asphalt tapered into a narrow lane until the bike abruptly swung left, diving onto a desolate unpaved dirt trail.

The sports car lunged after it. Plumes of dust billowed into the air, and loose gravel rattled violently against the chassis. After a frantic sprint, the motorcycle whipped around with a sharp skrrrt and slid to a halt. Construction barricades blocked the path entirely.

The sports car slammed its brakes, and almost instantly, a hulking thug kicked the driver’s door open, storming out with veins bulging on his neck. He sneered at the trapped biker.

"You fucking dead meat! You picked the wrong day to die, asshole!"

The brute reached inside his jacket and drew a sashimi knife. Tearing away the newspaper wrapped around the steel, the blade caught the afternoon sun with a blinding glint. The car undoubtedly belonged to Choi Ki-tae, but Ki-tae himself was nowhere in sight.

Moments later, the passenger door swung open. Jakyeong watched the second man step out with cold, calculating eyes.

He had bleached-blond hair, facial piercings through his lip and eyebrow, and a dokkaebi goblin tattoo inked in the exact same spot as Ki-tae’s. They didn't share a face, but they were almost certainly blood relatives or part of the same inner circle.

The enraged brute brandished the long blade, gesturing with a crooked finger. "Come on, pretty boy. Let me carve your guts out for you."

Jakyeong calmly pulled off his helmet, staring down the chuckling thug. A tactical black mask covered his face up to the bridge of his nose, rendering his identity completely unreadable.

"I said get over here, you little shit!"

Seeing the brute practically frothing at the mouth, Jakyeong took long, deliberate strides forward. Realizing this wasn't an apology walk, the thug lunged, slashing the knife in a vicious arc.

In one fluid motion, Jakyeong drew a suppressed pistol from his waistband and put a round straight through the man’s thigh.

Phfft.

A blood-curdling shriek tore through the air as the brute collapsed into the dirt, clutching his shattered leg and thrashing in agony.

"What the fuck—!"

Leaning against the car with a cigarette dangling from his lips, the blond thug reached frantically for his waistband—but Jakyeong was already a step ahead.

Phfft.

A round blew through the blond's shin, sending him crashing forward onto his knees. Jakyeong closed the distance in a heartbeat, pressing the warm suppressor dead-center against the man's forehead. Reaching behind the thug's lower back with his free hand, Jakyeong smoothly confiscated his sidearm, ejected the magazine, and hurled both into the tall grass.

"The kids you dragged back from the police station two days ago," Jakyeong said, his voice flat and arctic. "Where are they?"

The blond tilted his head up, his eyes rolling back in a defiant, feral grin. "Fuck you. You're that prick from the van. You think I’m gonna tell you shit?"

Before the sentence even finished landing, Jakyeong snapped his arm to the side, pointing the weapon at the wounded brute groaning in the dirt.

Without a fraction of a second's warning—Phfft.

The back of the brute's skull blew out in a violent spray, slamming his dead weight into the earth. Blood, bone fragments, and brain matter seeped into the dry soil, painting the ground a thick, muddy crimson.

Every drop of color instantly drained from the blond’s face.

"W-Wait... hold on! Don't! You don't know who the fuck you're messing with—you're making a massive mistake here!"

"Where are they?"

"Do you have any idea who my father is?! If you want something, we can negotiate! You don't have to be a savage—"

Jakyeong drew a combat dagger and drove the blade clean through the blond’s shoulder.

"AAAAAGH!"

A shrill, tearing scream shattered the quiet countryside. Steel sheared through muscle and ground brutally against the collarbone. As Jakyeong gave the hilt a slow, agonizing twist, the blond’s eyes rolled back until only the whites showed, white foam bubbling at the corners of his mouth.

Jakyeong paused the blade, looking down with dead, detached eyes.

"This is how I negotiate. Let's try the question again: Where are they?"

"Ugh... agh..."

"Still feel like keeping quiet?"

Tears of pure agony streamed down the man's bloodshot face as he shook his head frantically. "The... the warehouse..."

"Coordinates."

"If... if you let me live... I'll tell—"

Jakyeong twisted the blade another millimeter.

"I'LL TALK! IT'S THE SIHEUNG-DONG WAREHOUSE! AAAAAGH! FUCK! IT HURTS! I TOLD YOU! STOP! FUCK, PLEASE STOP!"

Jakyeong held out an open palm. "Phone. Hand it over."

Trembling violently, the man fished his smartphone from his pocket. Jakyeong bypassed the passcode and pulled up the contact list. Sure enough, Choi Ki-tae was pinned at the top, along with a recent message thread. Just as suspected: this punk was Ki-tae’s younger brother.

Jakyeong typed out a text:

[Hyung, what was the exact address of the warehouse in Siheung where we stashed the kids?]

He glanced down at the blond. Between the shattered leg and the pierced shoulder, the kid's face was turning an ashen gray, his breathing ragged and shallow.

Chime.

A reply popped up almost immediately:

[Are you fucking braindead? You got early-onset dementia or what? It's Doksan, not Siheung, you idiot.]

The corner of Jakyeong’s mouth ticked upward into a razor-thin smirk. The blond stared at the screen, sheer, suffocating terror creeping into his eyes.

"Your brother says you're lying."

"N-No! I mixed it up! It’s Doksan! Doksan! I remember now, I swear! 298-31 Doksan-dong!"

Without a heartbeat of hesitation, Jakyeong dialed Ki-tae’s number and hit speakerphone. After two rings, a gravelly, irritated voice barked through the line. Jakyeong held the mic inches from the blond's mouth.

Verify.

[The fuck do you want now, you little shit?!]

Staring down the black muzzle pressed against his brow, the blond forced his trembling lips to move. "H-Hyung... the place... where we're keeping the mules... it's 298-31 Doksan-dong, right?"

A heavy, exasperated sigh hissed through the speaker. But underneath the sigh, other sounds bled through—the wet, lewd slapping of skin against skin, accompanied by the muffled, breathy groans of a man. It took zero imagination to picture what Ki-tae was doing while taking this call.

The blond watched the phone with wide, terrified eyes, silently praying his brother wouldn't say the wrong thing.

[You fucking moron, how many times have you been there? Christ, you find new and creative ways to be a pain in my ass every damn day.]

"S-Sorry... I just blanked..."

[Hang up the damn phone. I'm busy.]

Click.

The line went dead. The blond let out a massive, shuddering breath of relief, looking up at Jakyeong with pleading eyes. There. I gave you what you wanted. You're going to spare me now, right?

Jakyeong slipped the phone into his tactical vest and pulled the trigger.

Phfft.

The back of the blond’s head burst open. His body slumped backward into the dirt, spattering fresh droplets of warm blood and tissue across Jakyeong’s mask.

Stepping over the corpse with unblinking indifference, Jakyeong walked over to the sports car. Using the reflection in the tinted glass, he wiped the blood off his face, then retrieved a compact C4 breaching charge from his sling bag and slapped the magnetic plate beneath the fuel tank.

He straddled the Kawasaki, fired up the engine, and tore back down the dirt path.

Seconds later, a muffled, concussive BOOM rattled the hills behind him. The stench of charred metal and copper lingered thick in the air.

Stepping out of his sedan, Kang Il-hyun took a deep, appreciative breath. The absence of neighboring properties meant the mountain air was exceptionally crisp. Building the estate out here really was the right call.

Walking through the main gates with a satisfied smile, he spotted two maintenance staff carrying an aluminum ladder out from behind the villa.

Setting the ladder down, the men bowed in unison. "Good evening, Executive Director."

"What's going on out here at this hour?"

"When the pool crew was moving heavy machinery earlier, they accidentally clipped one of the perimeter CCTV units. The angle shifted, so we just realigned it back to its original sweep."

Il-hyun had received word earlier that a construction truck had taken down a utility pole, causing a brief blackout. He’d put off installing a dedicated industrial backup generator, but it seemed he’d have to greenlight the requisition after all.

Dismissing the workers, Il-hyun strolled over to inspect the newly completed pool.

The dimensions and depth were immaculate. A pair of teak sun loungers sat neatly beside the water. He walked over, stretched his long legs out onto the cushions, and leaned back.

The night sky was unusually clear, blanketed in a brilliant dusting of stars. "Not bad," he murmured to himself. He couldn't wait for the basin to be filled so he could take a proper swim.

On the drive back from headquarters, a field report had come in: the owner of the private errand service and his entire staff had just surfaced as waterlogged corpses in a remote reservoir. It took no brilliance to deduce whose cleanup crew was responsible.

Missing the chance to interrogate them left a bitter, stinging annoyance in his gut. Kim Sun-young was probably cackling in triumph right about now. Treacherous old hag. That explained why she had strutted into his office with such arrogant confidence earlier today.

Scowling, Il-hyun shifted his gaze toward the second-floor guest wing.

The lights inside Jang Yi-an’s suite were completely dark. Asleep already?

He hadn't seen the boy’s face in two full days due to back-to-back corporate meetings, leaving him curiously eager to check in. The memory of the kid pinned beneath him—squirming in delicious humiliation while his waterline flushed a lewd, feverish red from raw arousal—had a habit of crossing his mind at the most unexpected moments.

Il-hyun pushed himself up from the lounger and entered the house. The senior housekeeper was already waiting in the foyer.

"Welcome home, Executive Director."

"Good evening. Any issues today?"

"Nothing aside from the brief power outage this afternoon. Ah, and Young Master Yi-an seemed to be coming down with a severe fever. He took some medication early in the evening and went straight to bed. He hasn't come down since."

Il-hyun’s brow furrowed. So that's why the suite is dark.

He turned toward the central staircase, but the housekeeper gently called out behind him.

"He specifically requested to rest without interruption tonight, sir. He asked me to pass that along to you."

In other words: tell Kang Il-hyun to stay out.

Pausing on the bottom step, Il-hyun considered the message for a second, then casually ignored it, taking the stairs two at a time.

Entering the guest suite, the motion-sensor lights in the private lounge illuminated softly. He crossed the floor to the master bedroom door—the room beyond was silent as a tomb.

He gave two firm knocks. Silence.

"Yi-an."

No response. He knocked again, harder this time. Still nothing.

He gripped the handle and twisted—locked from the inside.

Il-hyun’s eyes narrowed into sharp slits. Just as he was contemplating kicking the deadbolt off the frame, his smartphone buzzed in his palm.

[Director Kang. I've caught a terrible case of the flu and completely lost my voice. I'm so sorry, but I'll see you tomorrow.]

It was the very first text message he had ever received from Jang Yi-an.

Il-hyun stared down at the glowing screen, then back at the locked door. Another chime followed:

[I took my medicine. I think I just need to sleep it off. Thank you for your consideration.]

Il-hyun stared at the door for a beat, a faint, wry smile touching his lips.

"Get some rest, then."

No reply followed, nor did any further notifications light up the screen.

After lingering at the threshold for a few moments, Il-hyun finally turned and walked away. Dragging a sick man out of bed to torment him wasn't his style.

Though... it certainly would have been entertaining.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • Doksan-dong & Siheung-dong (독산동 / 시흥동): Neighboring industrial/residential districts located in Geumcheon-gu in southwestern Seoul. Known historically for dense factory clusters, logistics warehouses, and narrow alleyways, making them classic noir backdrops for illicit underground chop-shops and stash houses.

  • Sashimi Knife / Hoe-kal (회칼): Long, single-edged, razor-sharp Japanese-style slicing knives frequently carried by street-level Korean syndicate enforcers (kkakdugi) due to strict civilian firearm regulations in South Korea.
